# Memory

Create memory, and read and shape what it holds. Memory is known as looms in Maitento, which is why many of the calls start with `Loom`.

**Library:** [Maitento](index.md#maitento), for apps. More in [Memory](../../../concepts/memory.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`LoomCreate`](#loomcreate) | Creates a loom, a long-term memory for agents, and returns it as JSON. |
| [`LoomDelete`](#loomdelete) | Erases a loom and everything woven in it, for good. |
| [`LoomGet`](#loomget) | Finds a loom by its id or its name and returns it as JSON. |
| [`LoomList`](#loomlist) | Lists the looms in a namespace, sorted by name, as a JSON array. |
| [`LoomSeed`](#loomseed) | Copies the strongest shared knowledge of another loom into this one, and says how many threads it copied. |
| [`LoomSessions`](#loomsessions) | Lists the sessions agents have had with a loom, newest first, as a JSON array. |
| [`LoomUpdate`](#loomupdate) | Renames a loom, rewrites its description or changes its night-weaving settings, and returns the loom as JSON. |
| [`NightWeave`](#nightweave) | Asks for a loom to be night-woven now, without waiting for its quiet period. |
| [`NightWeavingList`](#nightweavinglist) | Lists a loom's night weavings, newest first, as a JSON array. |
| [`NightWeavingListSince`](#nightweavinglistsince) | Lists the night weavings of every loom in the tenant that changed at or after a given moment, oldest change first, as a JSON array. |
| [`PatternDelete`](#patterndelete) | Erases the pattern a loom keeps for a codebase. |
| [`PatternGet`](#patternget) | Returns the pattern a loom keeps for one codebase, as JSON. |
| [`PatternList`](#patternlist) | Lists the patterns a loom keeps, one per codebase, most recently changed first, as a JSON array. |
| [`PatternShape`](#patternshape) | Changes the pattern a loom keeps for a codebase, creating it if there is none, and returns the pattern as JSON. |
| [`ShuttleRetrieve`](#shuttleretrieve) | Searches a loom for the threads that matter to a question, best first, as a JSON array. |
| [`TapestryInspect`](#tapestryinspect) | Returns a loom's state as JSON: what it holds, what is held close, what is fading and what night weaving last did. |
| [`TapestryPanels`](#tapestrypanels) | Lists the portraits night weaving has written in a loom, one per person or thing, sorted by subject, as a JSON array. |
| [`TapestryReflect`](#tapestryreflect) | Gathers everything a loom holds about a topic, as JSON. |
| [`TapestryWeave`](#tapestryweave) | Writes the "What You Know" an agent would wake up with if the given people walked in now, and returns it as JSON. |
| [`TensionList`](#tensionlist) | Lists a loom's tensions, newest first, as a JSON array. |
| [`TensionResolve`](#tensionresolve) | Records how an open tension was resolved, and returns it with its two threads as JSON. |
| [`ThreadCut`](#threadcut) | Lets a thread go: its words are released, and a knot remains saying why. |
| [`ThreadGet`](#threadget) | Returns one thread of a loom as JSON. |
| [`ThreadGive`](#threadgive) | Gives a thread to another loom, where it arrives second-hand. |
| [`ThreadList`](#threadlist) | Lists a loom's threads, newest first unless sorted otherwise, as a JSON array. |
| [`ThreadPin`](#threadpin) | Pins a thread, so it is always part of what an agent wakes up knowing, or unpins it. |
| [`ThreadReframe`](#threadreframe) | Revises a thread: its wording, its weight, whether it is foundational, or the words it waits for. |
| [`ThreadUnravel`](#threadunravel) | Erases one thread for good, with any tension, portrait and pattern made from it. |
| [`ThreadWeave`](#threadweave) | Weaves a new thread into a loom, or strengthens the one it already has when it holds the same thing. |

### LoomCreate

Creates a loom, a long-term memory for agents, and returns it as JSON.

```c
jsonObject LoomCreate(string name, string namespace, string description)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The loom's name. |
| `namespace` | `string`, can be empty | The namespace to create it in, by id or name; `""` for the running app's namespace. |
| `description` | `string`, can be empty | What the loom is for; `""` for none. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The new loom, as JSON.

The loom starts empty, with night weaving on and a 15-minute quiet period; [`LoomUpdate`](#loomupdate) changes them. A loom declared in `looms/` is created by a deploy instead.

A name is 3 to 250 characters, cannot contain `@` or `/`, and must not already be used in the namespace (ignoring case). A description is at most 2,000 characters.

The loom's JSON holds `id`, `name`, `namespaceId`, `description`, `settings` (`nightWeaving`, `quietMinutes` and `weaverModel`, each null for its default), `lastWovenAt`, `lastActivityAt`, `lastNightWeavingAt`, `nightWeavingPending` and `dateCreated`.

Fails with "Namespace '…' not found" when no namespace has that name, and with "A loom named '…' already exists in this namespace" when the name is taken.

### LoomDelete

Erases a loom and everything woven in it, for good. There is no undo.

```c
void LoomDelete(string loomId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. A name is not accepted here. |

Everything goes: its threads, tensions, portraits, patterns, sessions and night-weaving records. This is erasure, for when data must be deleted. A loom never needs deleting to forget: threads that go unused fade, and [`ThreadCut`](#threadcut) lets one go.

Needs a tenant admin. The user the app runs as is checked when the call runs; if they are not an enabled tenant admin, the call fails with "LoomDelete erases loom data for good, so it needs a tenant admin: this app runs as a user who is not one." Maitento logs which user erased it.

### LoomGet

Finds a loom by its id or its name and returns it as JSON.

```c
jsonObject LoomGet(string loom)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loom` | `string` | The loom: its id, `name@namespace`, or its name in the running app's namespace. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The loom, as JSON.

`loom` is the loom's id; `name@namespace`, the namespace given by id or name; or a name alone, looked up in the running app's namespace. Names match ignoring case, and the names interactions give the looms they make for themselves, such as `wren-chat/Wren/Ana`, work too. When a name itself contains `@`, add `@namespace`: the last `@` is the separator.

The JSON is a loom as [`LoomCreate`](#loomcreate) describes it.

Fails with "No loom named '…' in the app's namespace" (or "in namespace '…'"), with "Namespace '…' not found", and, for an id, with "Loom … does not exist."

### LoomList

Lists the looms in a namespace, sorted by name, as a JSON array.

```c
jsonArray LoomList(string namespace)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `namespace` | `string`, can be empty | The namespace, by id or name; `""` for the running app's namespace. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of looms.

Each item is a loom as [`LoomCreate`](#loomcreate) describes it. The list includes the looms interactions made for themselves (named `interaction/seat/…`) as well as the ones declared in `looms/`. It holds at most 500 looms.

### LoomSeed

Copies the strongest shared knowledge of another loom into this one, and says how many threads it copied.

```c
jsonObject LoomSeed(string loomId, string fromLoom, string limit)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The id of the loom to copy into. |
| `fromLoom` | `string` | The loom to copy from, found as [`LoomGet`](#loomget) finds one: its id, `name@namespace`, or a name in the running app's namespace. |
| `limit` | `string`, can be empty | The most threads to copy, from 1 to 200; `""` for 200. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: What the seeding did, as JSON.

Only facts, how-tos and relationships travel (threads of kind `Semantic`, `Procedural` and `Relational`), and only shared ones: never a private note, an episode, a reflection, an intention or a cut thread. The heaviest go first. Each one arrives marked as inherited from `fromLoom`: as weft, unpinned, with a weight of at most 0.7 and no words to wait for. A thread the loom already holds is strengthened instead of copied, and one whose `until` date has passed stays behind.

Returns `{ loomId, fromLoomId, fromLoomName, inherited, alreadyKnown, withheld }`: how many threads were copied, how many the loom already knew, and how many were left behind.

Fails with "A loom cannot inherit from itself." and, for a limit out of range, with "Limit must be between 1 and 200".

### LoomSessions

Lists the sessions agents have had with a loom, newest first, as a JSON array.

```c
jsonArray LoomSessions(string loomId, string limit)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `limit` | `string`, can be empty | The most sessions to return, held between 1 and 500; `""` for 100. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of sessions.

A session is one agent's time with the loom in one interaction run. Each holds `interactionProcessId` (the run), `agentName`, `tapestry` (the "What You Know" it woke up with), `tapestryWovenAt`, `subjects` (who was present), `lastTurnAt`, `awaitingNight` (true until night weaving has consolidated it), `consolidatedByNightWeavingId`, and the ids of the threads it woke up knowing (`tapestryThreadIds`), was offered (`suggestedThreadIds`), recalled (`recalledThreadIds`) and wove (`wovenThreadIds`).

### LoomUpdate

Renames a loom, rewrites its description or changes its night-weaving settings, and returns the loom as JSON.

```c
jsonObject LoomUpdate(string loomId, string name, string description, string nightWeaving, string quietMinutes, string weaverModel, string clear)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `name` | `string`, can be empty | A new name; `""` to keep it. |
| `description` | `string`, can be empty | A new description, at most 2,000 characters; `""` to keep it. |
| `nightWeaving` | `string`, can be empty | `true` or `false`: whether night weaving tidies the loom up once it is quiet; `""` to keep it. |
| `quietMinutes` | `string`, can be empty | How many quiet minutes night weaving waits for, from 1 to 1,440; `""` to keep it. |
| `weaverModel` | `string`, can be empty | The name of the model night weaving thinks with, at most 200 characters; `""` to keep it. |
| `clear` | `string`, can be empty | What to return to its default, comma-separated or as a JSON array: `description` (none), `nightWeaving` (on), `quietMinutes` (15) or `weaverModel` (the agent's own model); `""` for nothing. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The loom as updated, as JSON.

Give only what you want to change: an empty argument keeps what is there. A setting you leave out keeps its value, so changing the quiet period leaves the weaver model as it is. To return something to its default, name it in `clear`; giving a value and clearing it in the same call is an error.

A loom an interaction made keeps the night-weaving settings it was created with, so this is how to change them for someone an agent has already met. A new name follows the rules of [`LoomCreate`](#loomcreate).

Fails with "Nothing to update: …" when every argument is empty, with "… was both given and cleared: do one or the other", and with "Quiet minutes must be between 1 and 1440 (a day)".

### NightWeave

Asks for a loom to be night-woven now, without waiting for its quiet period. It returns once the request is accepted; the weaving runs in the background.

```c
void NightWeave(string loomId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |

Night weaving tidies a loom up: it sums up each conversation, merges duplicates, notes contradictions and writes a portrait of each person. It thinks with the agent's model (or the loom's `weaverModel`), on the model keys of the last interaction run that used the loom, and costs about as much as one more reply. To see it finish, read [`NightWeavingList`](#nightweavinglist) until the newest night's `status` is `Completed` or `Failed`.

Fails when no interaction has used the loom yet, when night weaving is turned off for it, and when nothing has changed since its last night; the error says which.

### NightWeavingList

Lists a loom's night weavings, newest first, as a JSON array.

```c
jsonArray NightWeavingList(string loomId, string limit)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `limit` | `string`, can be empty | The most nights to return, held between 1 and 200; `""` for 20. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of night weavings.

Each night holds `id`, `loomId`, `status` (`Running`, `Completed` or `Failed`), `dateCreated`, `dateCompleted`, `counts` (what it did, such as `sessionsConsolidated`, `episodesWoven`, `threadsWoven`, `threadsMerged`, `tensionsFound` and `panelsWoven`), `dreamLog` (the weaver's journal entry for the night), `error` when it failed, and `tokenUsage`, one entry per model call.

### NightWeavingListSince

Lists the night weavings of every loom in the tenant that changed at or after a given moment, oldest change first, as a JSON array.

```c
jsonArray NightWeavingListSince(string since, string limit)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `since` | `string` | The moment to start from, in ISO 8601, such as `2026-11-02T09:00:00Z`. A time without an offset is UTC. |
| `limit` | `string`, can be empty | The most nights to return, held between 1 and 200; `""` for 20. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of night weavings.

Use it to add up what night weaving spent. Each night is as [`NightWeavingList`](#nightweavinglist) describes it. A night appears again each time it changes, so count each `tokenUsage` entry once, by its `turnId`. To read on, call again with the `dateUpdated` of the last night you got.

Fails with "since must be a date and time (ISO 8601), not '…'".

### PatternDelete

Erases the pattern a loom keeps for a codebase. There is no undo.

```c
void PatternDelete(string loomId, string codebase)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `codebase` | `string` | The codebase's name, matched ignoring case and extra spaces. |

To drop a single item instead, use [`PatternShape`](#patternshape) with `remove`. Erasing a pattern the loom does not keep does nothing.

Needs a tenant admin. The user the app runs as is checked when the call runs; if they are not an enabled tenant admin, the call fails with "PatternDelete erases loom data for good, so it needs a tenant admin: this app runs as a user who is not one." Maitento logs which user erased it.

### PatternGet

Returns the pattern a loom keeps for one codebase, as JSON.

```c
jsonObject PatternGet(string loomId, string codebase)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `codebase` | `string` | The codebase's name, matched ignoring case and extra spaces. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The pattern, as JSON.

A pattern is the shape of a codebase that agents work in, rather than facts about it: `architecture` (how it is built, in a few sentences), `heuristics` (how to find your way around), `keyFiles` (where to start) and `conventions`. Its JSON also holds `id`, `name`, `subjectKey`, `threadIds` (the threads night weaving refined it from), `lastChangedBy`, `revision` and `dateUpdated`. Agents keep patterns with their `LoomPattern` tool, and a pattern is woven into the tapestry when its codebase is in play.

Fails with "This loom keeps no pattern for …." when there is none.

### PatternList

Lists the patterns a loom keeps, one per codebase, most recently changed first, as a JSON array.

```c
jsonArray PatternList(string loomId, string limit)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `limit` | `string`, can be empty | The most patterns to return, held between 1 and 200; `""` for 50. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of patterns.

Each item is a pattern as [`PatternGet`](#patternget) describes it.

### PatternShape

Changes the pattern a loom keeps for a codebase, creating it if there is none, and returns the pattern as JSON.

```c
jsonObject PatternShape(string loomId, string codebase, string architecture, string heuristic, string keyFile, string convention, string remove)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `codebase` | `string` | The codebase's name. Case and extra spaces do not matter when finding its pattern. |
| `architecture` | `string`, can be empty | How the codebase is built, in a few sentences, replacing what is there; `""` to keep it. |
| `heuristic` | `string`, can be empty | One way to find your way around the codebase, to add; `""` for none. |
| `keyFile` | `string`, can be empty | One file to start from, to add; `""` for none. |
| `convention` | `string`, can be empty | One convention the codebase keeps, to add; `""` for none. |
| `remove` | `string`, can be empty | The start of the items to drop, from any list; `""` for none. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The pattern as shaped, as JSON.

Each argument is one change. An empty one is skipped, but at least one must be given. `architecture` replaces the summary. `heuristic`, `keyFile` and `convention` each add one item, unless the list already holds it (ignoring case). `remove` drops every item, from any list, whose text starts with it (ignoring case). The change is recorded as the app's.

A codebase name is at most 120 characters, an architecture at most 1,200 and an item at most 300; runs of spaces and line breaks in a name or an item become single spaces. Each list holds at most 20 items. Text that looks like a credential is refused. A pattern emptied of everything is removed.

Fails with "Say how to shape the pattern: …" when every change is empty, and with "This loom keeps no pattern for … yet, so there is nothing to remove or clear." when removing from a pattern that does not exist.

### ShuttleRetrieve

Searches a loom for the threads that matter to a question, best first, as a JSON array. It only looks: the threads it finds are not strengthened, as they are when an agent recalls them.

```c
jsonArray ShuttleRetrieve(string loomId, string query, string limit, string kinds, string about)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `query` | `string` | What to look for: a question, a topic or a name. |
| `limit` | `string`, can be empty | The most threads to return, held between 1 and 50; `""` for 8. |
| `kinds` | `string`, can be empty | Only threads of these kinds, comma-separated or as a JSON array: `Semantic`, `Episodic`, `Relational`, `Procedural`, `Reflection` or `Intention`; `""` for every kind. |
| `about` | `string`, can be empty | The people or things present, comma-separated or as a JSON array (up to 8): threads about them rank higher. `""` for nobody in particular. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of results.

This is the search an agent's `LoomRecall` tool makes. Threads are found by meaning when the tenant has an OpenAI model key, and by their words otherwise. Private notes are searched too.

Each result is `{ thread, relevance, semantic, lexical, context, companionOf }`: the thread, as [`ThreadGet`](#threadget) describes it; `relevance`, its overall score from 0 to 1; `semantic` and `lexical`, how close its meaning and its words are to the query; `context`, 1 when it is about someone in `about`; and `companionOf`, set when it came back alongside another thread it is often used with.

A query is at most 2,000 characters.

### TapestryInspect

Returns a loom's state as JSON: what it holds, what is held close, what is fading and what night weaving last did.

```c
jsonObject TapestryInspect(string loomId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The loom's state, as JSON.

The JSON holds `loom`, as [`LoomCreate`](#loomcreate) describes it; `tally`, the thread counts (`threads`, `warp`, `weft`, `knots`, `pinned`, `private` and `byKind`); `pinned`, up to 10 threads held close; `recentlyAccessed`, up to 5; `highWeightDormant`, up to 5 important threads unused for over 30 days; `fraying`, up to 5 threads loosening through disuse; `openTensions`, up to 5, as [`TensionList`](#tensionlist) describes them; `lastNightWeaving`, the last completed night with its dream log, or null; `panelSubjects`, who has a portrait; and `patterns`, the codebases it keeps a pattern for. Looking changes nothing.

### TapestryPanels

Lists the portraits night weaving has written in a loom, one per person or thing, sorted by subject, as a JSON array.

```c
jsonArray TapestryPanels(string loomId, string limit)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `limit` | `string`, can be empty | The most portraits to return, held between 1 and 500; `""` for 100. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of portraits.

A portrait (a panel) is short prose about one subject. It goes at the top of the tapestry when its subject is present, and is rewritten when the threads about that subject change. Each holds `subject`, `subjectKey` (the subject in lower case, for matching), `text`, `threadIds` (the threads it was written from) and `nightWeavingId`.

### TapestryReflect

Gathers everything a loom holds about a topic, as JSON. It only looks: nothing is strengthened.

```c
jsonObject TapestryReflect(string loomId, string topic)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `topic` | `string` | What to reflect on: a topic, a person or a question. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: What the loom holds about the topic, as JSON.

This is what an agent's `LoomReflect` tool gathers. The JSON holds `topic`; `warp`, the foundational threads about it; `weft`, the other threads, grouped by kind, strongest first; `tensions`, open tensions among them, as [`TensionList`](#tensionlist) describes them; `knots`, threads that were let go, and why; `changed`, threads that were reframed, whose `seams` show how understanding moved; and `isEmpty`, true when the loom holds nothing about it. It brings back up to 24 threads, 8 knots and 10 tensions.

A topic is at most 2,000 characters.

### TapestryWeave

Writes the "What You Know" an agent would wake up with if the given people walked in now, and returns it as JSON. It starts no session and changes no thread.

```c
jsonObject TapestryWeave(string loomId, string about, string agentName, string tokens)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `about` | `string`, can be empty | The people or things present, comma-separated or as a JSON array (up to 8); `""` for nobody in particular. |
| `agentName` | `string`, can be empty | The seat name of the agent waking up, whose own private notes are then included; `""` for shared threads only. |
| `tokens` | `string`, can be empty | The most tokens the tapestry may take, held between 200 and 20,000; `""` for 1,500. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The tapestry, as JSON.

Use it to see what a run will know before it starts. The JSON is `{ loomId, agentName, subjects, tokenBudget, text, threadIds, isEmptyLoom }`: `text` is the tapestry exactly as it would sit in the agent's instructions, `threadIds` the threads it was woven from, and `isEmptyLoom` true when the loom holds nothing yet.

### TensionList

Lists a loom's tensions, newest first, as a JSON array. A tension is two threads that pull against each other.

```c
jsonArray TensionList(string loomId, string includeResolved, string limit)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `includeResolved` | `string`, can be empty | `true` to include resolved tensions as well; `""` for open tensions only. |
| `limit` | `string`, can be empty | The most tensions to return, held between 1 and 250; `""` for 100. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of tensions.

Each item is `{ tension, thread1, thread2 }`. The `tension` holds `id`, `kind` (`Contradicts`, `Supersedes` or `Diverges`), `note` (what it is, in a sentence), `threadId1`, `threadId2`, `isOpen` and, once it is resolved, `dateResolved`, `resolution` and `resolvedBy`. `thread1` and `thread2` are the two threads, or null once a thread has been erased.

### TensionResolve

Records how an open tension was resolved, and returns it with its two threads as JSON.

```c
jsonObject TensionResolve(string loomId, string tensionId, string resolution)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `tensionId` | `string` | The tension's id, from [`TensionList`](#tensionlist). |
| `resolution` | `string` | How it was resolved, in a sentence or two. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The resolved tension with its threads, as JSON.

Neither thread changes: to correct one, use [`ThreadReframe`](#threadreframe) or [`ThreadCut`](#threadcut) as well. The resolution is recorded as the app's. The JSON is as [`TensionList`](#tensionlist) describes an item.

A resolution is at most 2,000 characters. Fails with "Tension … was already resolved: …" and with "There is no tension … in this loom."

### ThreadCut

Lets a thread go: its words are released, and a knot remains saying why. Returns the thread as JSON.

```c
jsonObject ThreadCut(string loomId, string threadId, string acknowledgment, string essence)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `threadId` | `string` | The thread's id. |
| `acknowledgment` | `string` | Why it is being let go. |
| `essence` | `string`, can be empty | What is worth keeping of it; `""` for nothing. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The thread, now a knot, as JSON: `knot` holds what remains.

This is forgetting, not erasure. The knot keeps the date, `acknowledgment`, any `essence` and who cut it, and [`ThreadList`](#threadlist) shows knots when asked to. The thread's `content` becomes empty, it is unpinned, and agents no longer know it. To remove a thread completely, use [`ThreadUnravel`](#threadunravel).

Fails with "Thread … was already let go." for a thread that was already cut.

### ThreadGet

Returns one thread of a loom as JSON. Looking at it does not strengthen it.

```c
jsonObject ThreadGet(string loomId, string threadId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `threadId` | `string` | The thread's id. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The thread, as JSON.

A thread is one memory. Its JSON holds `id`, `content`, `kind`, `strand` (`Warp`, foundational and never fading, or `Weft`), `weight` and `fray` (each from 0 to 1), `salience` (its standing: its weight, loosened by fraying), `subjects`, `tags`, `cues` (the words it waits for), `visibility` (`Shared` or `Private`), `basis` (`Said`, `Impression` or `Read`), `until`, `pinned`, `origin` (who wove it), `provenance` (set when it came from another loom), `knot` (set once it is cut), `seams` (one for each reframe), `accessCount`, `lastAccessedAt`, `reinforcements`, `shortId` (the 8 characters agents see), `revision` and `dateCreated`.

Fails with "There is no thread … in this loom." when the thread is not in this loom.

### ThreadGive

Gives a thread to another loom, where it arrives second-hand. Returns `{ thread, reinforced }` as JSON.

```c
jsonObject ThreadGive(string loomId, string threadId, string toLoom, string note)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The id of the loom the thread is in. |
| `threadId` | `string` | The thread's id. |
| `toLoom` | `string` | The loom to give it to, found as [`LoomGet`](#loomget) finds one: its id, `name@namespace`, or a name in the running app's namespace. |
| `note` | `string`, can be empty | What to say with it, kept with the thread; `""` for nothing. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The thread in the receiving loom and whether it was already known, as JSON.

The receiving loom's agents are told they know it second-hand ("an app told you"), and its `provenance` says where it came from. It arrives as weft, unpinned, with a weight of at most 0.7 and no words to wait for. `thread` is the thread in the receiving loom; `reinforced` is true when that loom already held it and its own thread was strengthened instead.

Only shared knowledge travels: a private note, an episode, a reflection, an intention, a cut thread or one whose `until` has passed cannot be given, and the error says why. A note is at most 500 characters. Fails with "That loom already holds it: a gift goes to a different loom." when both looms are the same.

### ThreadList

Lists a loom's threads, newest first unless sorted otherwise, as a JSON array. Listing never strengthens a thread.

```c
jsonArray ThreadList(string loomId, string kinds, string strand, string knots, string pinned, string subject, string limit, string sort, string skip)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `kinds` | `string`, can be empty | Only threads of these kinds, comma-separated or as a JSON array: `Semantic`, `Episodic`, `Relational`, `Procedural`, `Reflection` or `Intention`; `""` for every kind. |
| `strand` | `string`, can be empty | `warp` or `weft`, for only threads of that strand; `""` for both. |
| `knots` | `string`, can be empty | `exclude`, `include` or `only`; `""` for `exclude`. |
| `pinned` | `string`, can be empty | `true` for pinned threads only, `false` for unpinned ones only; `""` for both. |
| `subject` | `string`, can be empty | Only threads about this person or thing, matched ignoring case and extra spaces; `""` for all. |
| `limit` | `string`, can be empty | The most threads to return, held between 1 and 500; `""` for 50. |
| `sort` | `string`, can be empty | `newest`, `weight`, `recently-accessed` or `most-frayed`; `""` for `newest`. |
| `skip` | `string`, can be empty | How many threads to skip first, held between 0 and 10,000; `""` for none. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of threads.

Private notes are included. Cut threads (knots) are left out unless `knots` asks for them. Each item is a thread as [`ThreadGet`](#threadget) describes it. Page through a large loom with `skip` and `limit`. The words in `strand`, `knots` and `sort` match ignoring case.

### ThreadPin

Pins a thread, so it is always part of what an agent wakes up knowing, or unpins it. Returns the thread as JSON.

```c
jsonObject ThreadPin(string loomId, string threadId, string pinned)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `threadId` | `string` | The thread's id. |
| `pinned` | `string`, can be empty | `false` to unpin it; `""` or `true` to pin it. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The thread, as JSON.

A cut thread cannot be pinned or unpinned, and an intention cannot be pinned: it waits for its words instead. Pinning a thread that is already pinned changes nothing.

### ThreadReframe

Revises a thread: its wording, its weight, whether it is foundational, or the words it waits for. Returns the thread as JSON.

```c
jsonObject ThreadReframe(string loomId, string threadId, string reason, string content, string weight, string foundational, string acknowledgment, string remindWhen)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `threadId` | `string` | The thread's id. |
| `reason` | `string` | Why it is changing; the seam keeps it. |
| `content` | `string`, can be empty | New wording; `""` to keep it. |
| `weight` | `string`, can be empty | A new weight, from 0 to 1; `""` to keep it. |
| `foundational` | `string`, can be empty | `true` to make it warp (foundational: it never fades), `false` to make it weft; `""` to keep it. |
| `acknowledgment` | `string`, can be empty | Needed when revising a warp thread or making one: say plainly that a foundation is being changed, and why. `""` otherwise. |
| `remindWhen` | `string`, can be empty | The words it should wait for, replacing the ones it has, comma-separated or as a JSON array; `none` clears them, and `""` keeps them. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The thread as revised, as JSON.

Every reframe leaves a seam on the thread that keeps what it said before, its weight and strand, and why it changed, so you can see how understanding moved. Give at least one change, and the reason.

Foundations are protected: revising a warp thread, or making a thread warp, needs `acknowledgment`. A cut thread cannot be reframed (weave a new one), and an intention cannot become foundational or be left with no words to wait for.

Content is at most 4,000 characters, and text that looks like a credential is refused.

### ThreadUnravel

Erases one thread for good, with any tension, portrait and pattern made from it. There is no undo.

```c
void ThreadUnravel(string loomId, string threadId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `threadId` | `string` | The thread's id. |

This is erasure, for when data must be deleted. To let a thread go and keep a note of why, use [`ThreadCut`](#threadcut).

Needs a tenant admin. The user the app runs as is checked when the call runs; if they are not an enabled tenant admin, the call fails with "ThreadUnravel erases loom data for good, so it needs a tenant admin: this app runs as a user who is not one." Maitento logs which user erased it.

### ThreadWeave

Weaves a new thread into a loom, or strengthens the one it already has when it holds the same thing. Returns `{ thread, reinforced }` as JSON.

```c
jsonObject ThreadWeave(string loomId, string content, string kind, string weight, string about, string tags, string foundational, string private, string pinned, string remindWhen, string until, string basis)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `loomId` | `string` | The loom's id. |
| `content` | `string` | What to remember, in words that will make sense on their own later. |
| `kind` | `string`, can be empty | `Semantic` (a fact or preference), `Episodic` (something that happened), `Relational` (who someone is), `Procedural` (how to do something), `Reflection` (a note to self) or `Intention` (something to do when its moment comes); `""` for `Semantic`. |
| `weight` | `string`, can be empty | How much it matters, from 0 to 1; `""` for 0.5. |
| `about` | `string`, can be empty | Who or what it is about, comma-separated or as a JSON array; `""` for no one. |
| `tags` | `string`, can be empty | Free-form tags, comma-separated or as a JSON array; `""` for none. |
| `foundational` | `string`, can be empty | `true` makes it warp (foundational: it never fades), `false` makes it weft; `""` for warp only when it is `Relational`. |
| `private` | `string`, can be empty | `true` makes it a private note; `""` for shared. |
| `pinned` | `string`, can be empty | `true` pins it, so it is always part of what an agent wakes up knowing; `""` for unpinned. |
| `remindWhen` | `string`, can be empty | The words that bring it back to an agent when someone says them, comma-separated or as a JSON array; `""` for none. |
| `until` | `string`, can be empty | When it stops holding: a day such as `2026-11-30` (it holds until that day is over), or a date and time; `""` to hold until it is let go. |
| `basis` | `string`, can be empty | `said` (someone said it), `impression` (the app's own reading) or `read` (learned from a document or a tool); `""` for `said`. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The thread that now holds it and whether it was already known, as JSON.

This is what an agent's `LoomWeave` tool does; the thread is recorded as woven by the app. When the loom already holds the same thing, in nearly the same words or (with an OpenAI model key) the same meaning, that thread is strengthened instead and `reinforced` is true.

By default a thread is `Semantic`, weighs 0.5, is shared and unpinned, rests on what was `said`, and is warp only when it is `Relational`. An `impression` or something `read` is held loosely: it weighs at most 0.4 and is never foundational. An `Intention` needs `remindWhen`, and cannot be foundational, pinned, or rest on anything but what was said.

A private thread is a note that only the agent that wove it can see, so one an app weaves is seen by no agent: only apps and the API can read it.

Content is at most 4,000 characters, and text that looks like a credential is refused. Up to 8 subjects and 12 tags are kept. `until` must be in the future.
